en: Record of the Items Brought Back from Taizhou by Dainichi Nitchū (Saichō).

Compiled by Saichō and others. Catalogue of the Combined Commentaries and Records. Among the one hundred and two works totaling two hundred and forty fascicles compiled by the Japanese monk Saichō and others who sought the Dharma, there is additionally one scroll of silk illustrations;
the commentaries consist of six lines per sheet, totaling eight hundred and ninety-seven sheets of paper.

*The Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra* (Miaofa lianhua jing xuanyi), ten fascicles; expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, totaling 272 sheets. *Commentary on the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra* (Xuanyi shi), ten fascicles; composed by the Venerable Jingxi, totaling 343 sheets.
*Sub-commentary on the Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sutra* (Wenju shu), ten fascicles; expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, totaling 337 sheets.

*Recorded Notes on the Sub-commentary on the Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sutra* (Wenju shu ji), ten fascicles; composed by the Venerable Jingxi, totaling 515 sheets. *Contemplation of the Lotus Sutra* (Fahua guan)... [text fragment]

*Yinpǐnyì* (Meaning of the "Expedient Means" Chapter), one fascicle; produced by the Great Master Zhizhe, forty sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing Guanyinpǐnyìshū* (Commentary on the Meaning of the "Avalokiteśvara" Chapter of the Lotus Sutra), two fascicles;

produced by the Great Master Zhizhe, thirty-eight sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing kēwén* (Outline of the Lotus Sutra), two fascicles; composed by Venerable Zuoxi, eighty-five sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing Guanyinpǐn jìkēwén* (Verses and Outline of the "Avalokiteśvara" Chapter of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle;
one sheet. *Miaofa lianhua jing dàyì* (General Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle; narrated by Preceptor Mingkuang of Jingxi, ten sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing* (The Lotus Sutra).

*Jingwenju xu* (Preface to the Textual Phrases), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Shenhui of Kuaiji, three sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing chanfa* (Repentance Rite of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle; also titled *Sanmei xingfa* (Method for Practicing Samādhi), compiled by the Great Master Zhizhe, eighteen sheets.

*Miaofa lianhua jing sanmei bubozhi yi* (Supplementary Ritual for the Samādhi of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle; composed by the Venerable Jingxi, three sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing dayi* (General Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle, five sheets.

*Miaofa lianhua jing xuanyi kewen* (Outline of the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle, seven sheets. *Miaofa lianhua jing wenju shu* (Commentary on the Textual Phrases of the Lotus Sutra).
*Ke-wen* (Outline), one fascicle, six sheets. The above eleven works, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Mo-ho chih-kuan), ten fascicles; compiled by the Great Master Chih-i, three hundred and seventy sheets. *Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā Supplemented Practice, Transmission, and Resolution of Doubts* (Mo-ho chih-kuan pu-hsing ch’uan-hung chüeh), ten fascicles;

composed by Master Jingxi [Zhanran], seven hundred and forty-seven sheets. *Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā Wén-jù* (Commentary on the Text), two fascicles; composed by Master Jingxi, seventy-eight sheets. *Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā Yì* (Meaning/Principles).
Example Two: *The Essential Heart of the Mohe Zhiguan*, compiled by Master Jingxi, thirty-one pages; *The Phonetic Commentary on the Mohe Zhiguan*, one volume, eight pages;
*The Abridged Phonetic Commentary on the Mohe Zhiguan*, one volume, fifteen pages; *The General Meaning of the Mohe Zhiguan*, compiled by Master Jingxi, ten pages;
*The General Meaning of the Eight Teachings of the Mohe Zhiguan*, composed by the Śramaṇa Mingkuang of Jingxi, fifteen pages; *The Structural Outline of the Mohe Zhiguan*, one volume, eight pages.
One chart of the Three Virtues from the *Mohe zhiguan* (Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā), comprising six sheets; the above nine sections totaling ten fascicles are contained in one volume.

The *Chanwen xiuzheng* (Texts on Meditation and Realization) in ten fascicles, produced by Master Zhizhe, comprises one hundred and seventy-nine sheets. The *Chanmen zhang* (Chapter on the Gate of Meditation) in one fascicle, produced by Master Zhizhe, comprises fifty-nine sheets.

The *Chanmen yaolüe* (Essentials of the Gate of Meditation) in one fascicle, produced by Master Zhizhe, comprises five sheets. The *Xiuxian liunmiaomen* (Six Sublime Gates of Cultivating Meditation) in one fascicle, produced by Master Zhizhe, comprises thirteen sheets.

*Changuan chanyao fangbian famen* (Oral Instructions on the Methods for Expediently Practicing Dhyāna), one fascicle; expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, nine pages. *Sishanchu* (Four Foundations of Mindfulness), four fascicles; compiled by Upādhyāya Zhiyan, sixty-eight pages.

*Guansin lun* (Treatise on Contemplating the Mind), one fascicle; expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, nine pages. *Guansin lun shu* (Commentary on the Treatise on Contemplating the Mind), two fascicles;

compiled by Upādhyāya Zhiyan, eighty-six pages. *Xiaozhiguan* (Minor Stopping and Contemplation), one fascicle; upper fascicle, expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, seventeen pages. *Jueyi sanmei* (Samādhi of the Awakening Mind), one fascicle; expounded by the Great Master Zhizhe, nineteen pages. *Zaguangxing* (Miscellaneous Contemplative Practices), one fascicle.

*One fascicle of the Record of the Eight-Page *Guanjing* Recitation Ritual*, compiled by the Great Master Zhiyi; *One fascicle of the Golden Light Repentance Method*, five pages, compiled by Upādhyāya Jingxi;

*One fascicle of the Supplementary Ritual for the Four-Page Vaipulya Repentance*, three pages, compiled by Upādhyāya Jingxi. The above fourteen works, totaling seventeen fascicles, are contained in this single volume.

The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra Xuanshu* (Profound Commentary) in six fascicles, consisting of one hundred and sixteen sheets, was produced by Master Zhizhe. The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra Shuji* (Commentary-Record) in three or six fascicles, consisting of one hundred and forty-eight sheets, was composed by Upādhyāya Jingxi. These two works, totaling nine fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra-brief-commentary* (10 fascicles), compiled by the Venerable Jingxi; 394 sheets. *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra-commentary-private-records* (3 fascicles), the first fascicle of which contains the *Xuan-yi* (Profound Meaning) compiled by the Dharma-transmitting disciple Daoyou;
148 sheets. *Fourfold Teaching Ritual* (12 fascicles), established by the Great Master Zhizhe;
97 sheets. *Text on the Vow*, spoken by the Great Master Nanyue Huisi; 14 sheets. *Ritual for the Forty-two Holy Sages*, compiled by the Venerable Jingxi; 3 sheets. *Nirvāṇa*... [text truncated]

*Ban houfen kewen* (Outline of the Latter Part of the *Bannian*), one fascicle, composed by Master Jingxi; six sheets. *Wufangbian yi* (Meaning of the Five Expedient Means), one fascicle, expounded by Master Zhizhe; one sheet. *Shibunermen yi* (Meaning of the Ten Gates of Non-duality), one fascicle.

*Tiantai Shan Guoqing Si bailu* (The Hundred Records of Guoqing Monastery on Mount Tiantai), five fascicles. *Mount Tiantai Master Zhizhe Lingying tu* (Illustrations of the Miraculous Responses of Master Zhizhe at Mount Tiantai), one image.

*Mount Tiantai Guoqing Si bi shang dashi shuo fa yingxiang bing Foting ji Weimo siwang liuzu xiang* (The Image of the Master Preaching the Dharma on the Wall of Guoqing Monastery at Mount Tiantai, along with the Buddha-Usnīṣa, Vimalakīrti, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the Six Patriarchs), one fascicle, composed by Yan Zhenqing; eleven sheets.

*The Separate Biography of the Great Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, composed by the śramaṇa Dào Zhèng; twelve sheets. *Eulogy of the Great Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle; three sheets.
*Epitaph for the Tomb of the Great Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, composed by the Layman Cilì Mǎ Duì; five sheets.

*Left Epitaph Before the Tomb of the Great Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, composed by Wàn Qíróng, a mountain man of Shànghuáng in Kuàijī; five sheets. *Right Epitaph Before the Tomb of the Great Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle.

One scroll, *The Separate Biography of the Great Master Zhizhe of Mount Tiantai*, compiled by Dharma Master Lun of Longquan Temple, five sheets. One scroll, *A Brief Biography of the Sixth Patriarch of Mount Tiantai*, compiled by the Śramaṇa Fanniao, seven sheets.
One scroll, *The Biography of the Fifth Patriarch, Venerable Zuoxi of Mount Tiantai*, compiled by Vinaya Master Xuán of Zhongnan Mountain and others, seven sheets.

One scroll, *The Stele Inscription for the Sixth Patriarch, Venerable Jingxi of Mount Tiantai*, composed by the Proofreader Ān Ding, five sheets. [One scroll], *The Biography of the Great Master Zhizhe of Mount Tiantai*, five sheets.
*Record of the Fulong Daochang*, one scroll, composed by Liang Su of Anding; nine sheets. *Stele of Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai*, one scroll, composed by Li Yong;
seven sheets. *Stele of Shiquan at Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai*, one scroll; five sheets. *Separate Biography of Master Si of Nanyue*, one scroll; five sheets.

*Biographies of Eminent Monks of Nanyue*, one scroll, composed by Lu Zangyong, Attendant-in-Ordinary; fifteen sheets. *Record of Nanyue*, one scroll, composed by Li Yong; three sheets. *Combined Record of Nanyue and Mount Tiantai*, one scroll.

*The Separate Biography of the Great Master Zhizhe of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, five sheets; compiled by Liang Su. *The Separate Biographies of the Twelve Disciples of Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets.
*The Text and Commentary on the Meaning of Samādhi in Study*, one fascicle, ten sheets; compiled by Upādhyāya Jingxi. The above two works comprise seven fascicles in one volume.

*The Profound Meaning of the Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, forty-seven sheets; compiled by Upādhyāya Zhang’an. *The Commentary on the Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, fifteen fascicles, four hundred and eighty-three sheets; compiled by Upādhyāya Zhang’an. The above two works comprise sixteen fascicles in one volume.

*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*, fifteen fascicles; revised by Master Jingxi, five hundred and eighty-nine sheets. *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śabdavyākhyāna-vidhi*, one fascicle; compiled by Fashuan, thirty-seven sheets. *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra-privata-ki*, ten fascicles; compiled by the Dharma-transmitting disciple Daosui, three hundred and eighty-three sheets. *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śabdavyākhyāna*, one fascicle, twenty-eight sheets. *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra-chao*, five fascicles, three hundred and thirty-six sheets. *Konggangbei-lun* (The Diamond Scalpel Treatise), one fascicle; composed by Master Jingxi, fifteen sheets. *Konggangbei-lun-ji* (Record of the Diamond Scalpel Treatise), recorded by the Jingxi śramaṇa Mingkuang, eighteen sheets. *Konggangbei-lun-kewen* (Outline of the Diamond Scalpel Treatise), one fascicle. The above seven works, totaling twenty fascicles, share one volume. The *Nirvāṇa* section comprises one thousand eight hundred and thirty-seven sheets.

*Huayan jing gumu* (Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), one fascicle, compiled by Master Jingxi; fifty-eight pages. *Fajie cidi* (The Successive Stages of the Dharma Realm), three fascicles, expounded by Master Zhiyi;

eighty pages. *Anle xing* (The Course of Ease and Bliss), one fascicle, spoken by Master Nanyue Huisi; thirteen pages. *Jinguangming jing xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Golden Light Sūtra), one fascicle, expounded by Master Zhiyi;

twenty-six pages. *Jinguangming jing shu* (Commentary on the Golden Light Sūtra), three fascicles, expounded by Master Zhiyi; eighty-nine pages. *Bosha jie jing yiji* (Record of the Meaning of the Bodhisattva Precepts Sūtra), two fascicles, [expounded by] Master Zhiyi.

One fascicle of the *Commentary on the Sutra of the Dharani for Invoking Avalokiteśvara*, consisting of forty-four pages, expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi; one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Sutra of Immeasurable Life*, consisting of fourteen pages, expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi;

one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra*, consisting of twenty-four pages, expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi; and one fascicle of the *Resolution of Ten Doubts regarding the Amitābha Sutra*, consisting of five pages, expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi.
These ten works, totaling fifteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Meaning of the Six Stages of Attainment in the Perfect Teaching*, one fascicle; expounded by Master Zhizhe, five sheets. *The Meaning of the Six Stages of Attainment*, one fascicle; four sheets.
*The Text for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle; spoken by Master Nanyue, seven sheets.
*The Text for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle; compiled by Upādhyāya Jingxi, ten sheets. *The Seven-Day Method of Repentance*, one fascicle; fourteen sheets.
*The General Meaning of the Tiantai School*, one fascicle, three pages; *Praise for Mount Tiantai*, one fascicle, three pages, composed by Upādhyāya Zhāng'ān;
*Diagram of the Three Periods of the Lotus Sūtra*, one fascicle, six pages; *Wei Xūzhōu’s Text on Judging the Dispute over the Four Teachings of Tiantai*, one fascicle, one page;
*Petitions for the Dharma-Seeking Feast from the Kingdom of Japan*, one fascicle, seven items, ten pages.
One scroll of the *Catalogue of the Quest for the Dharma in the Kingdom of Japan*, comprising fourteen sheets;
among the thirty-eight works totaling forty scrolls above, one silk painting is included, making forty-one scrolls in total.
The Tiantai Catalogue of Missing Texts, including commentaries and exegeses, comprises fourteen works in forty-one fascicles.

The *Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in four fascicles; the *Commentary on the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Commentary on the Maitreya’s Buddhahood Sūtra* in five fascicles; the *Commentary on the Śāstra* (Vasubandhu’s *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā*) in twenty fascicles; the *Meaning of the Three Contemplations* in two fascicles; the *Explanation of the Meaning of All Scriptures through the Contemplation of the Mind* in one fascicle; the *Explanation of the Meaning of the Ten Suchnesses* in one fascicle; the *Profound Meaning of the Explanation of All Scriptures* produced by the Great Master Zhiyi in one fascicle; the *Meaning of the Seven Learners* produced by the Great Master Zhiyi in one fascicle; the *Meaning of the Seven Expedient Means* produced by the Great Master Zhiyi in one fascicle; the *Meaning of the One, Two, Three, and Four Bodies* produced by the Great Master Zhiyi in one fascicle; the *Brief Cessation and Contemplation* in one fascicle (fascicle lower); the *Contemplation of the Mind for Reciting the Twelve Divisions of the Dharma* in one fascicle; and the *Practice Method for the Pratyutpanna Samādhi* in one fascicle. The above comprise the commentaries and their respective meanings.
Fourteen works in forty-one fascicles.
In the twenty-second year of the Kaiyuan era,
Dharma Master Cen of Longquan Temple, together with the monk Daomou, [compiled this].
Although the titles of these works appear on the right pillar of the monument erected before the tomb of the Great Master Zhi,
the Liang dynasty versions have not yet been obtained.

The *Tiantai Suibu Mulü* (Catalogue of the Tiantai Supplementary Sections) comprises fifteen categories, including the "Combined Miscellaneous Meanings" (*Hezayi*) and others. One category, the "Meaning of the Three Contemplations" (*Sanguanyiyi*), is included in the *Zhi Guan Bu* (Section on Stopping and Contemplation).

One category, the "Explanation of the Twenty-five Samādhis" (*Shierwushanmeiyiyi*), is included in the *Sijiaoyi* (Meaning of the Four Teachings) and the *Fahua Xuanyi Bu* (Section on the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra).
One category, the "Meaning of the Four Kinds of Samādhis" (*Sanzhongsanmeiyiyi*), is included in the *Zhi Guan Bu*. The fourth [category]... [text ends].

The section on the meaning of the Four Noble Truths is included in the *Fahua xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra); the section on the sevenfold meaning of the Two Truths is included in the *Fahua xuanyi*;

the section on the Three Truths is included in the *Fahua xuanyi*; the section on the four gates of meaning is included in the *Sijiaoyi* (Meaning of the Four Teachings), as well as the *Zhi guan* (Stopping and Seeing), the *Xuanlun* (Treatise on Profundity), the *Fahua jing* (Lotus Sutra), the *Weimojie jing* (Vimalakīrti Sutra), and other related sections; and the section on the meaning of the four lands is included in the same works.

One section is included in the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-ṭīkā* (Commentary on the Vimalakīrti): the meaning of the four non-arising (*catur-anutpāda*). One section is included in the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-ṭīkā*, the *Śamatha-vipaśyanā*, and related works: the meaning of the four *siddhāntas*.
One section is included in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-mahā-arthavyākhyāna* (Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), the *Catuḥprakaraṇa-artha* (Meaning of the Four Teachings), and related works:

the meaning of the ten dharma-realms (*daśa-dharmadhātu*). One section is included in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-mahā-arthavyākhyāna*, the *Catuḥprakaraṇa-artha*, and related works: the ten dharmas that constitute the vehicle (*daśa-dharma-yāna-saṃgraha*).

The fifteen sections of doctrine listed above include: the *Yi-yi-ke-ru-zhi-guan-deng-bu* (Section on the Meaning of Entering into Stopping and Contemplation and Other Categories), the *Qing-guan-yin-san-mei-xing-fa* (Ritual for the Practice of the Samādhi of Invoking Avalokiteśvara) in one fascicle, the *Ru-zhi-guan* (Entering into Stopping and Contemplation) together with the *Tiantai Guoqing Bai-lu-bu* (Section from the Hundred Records of Tiantai Guoqing Temple), and the *Fangdeng-san-mei-fa* (Method of the Vaipulya Samādhi) in one fascicle, also included in the *Ru-zhi-guan* and the *Tiantai Guoqing Bai-lu-bu*. These constitute the fifteen sections of doctrine.
Following the Great Master Zhizhe,
this is the private record of Upādhyāya Zhang’an;
its meanings have been organized into fascicles according to their respective topics.
The records made previously and subsequently are scattered across various regions;
fearing that later students might harbor doubts, [I have compiled them here].
In the *Longquan ji* (Record of the Dragon Spring),
the titles are preserved as they were among the various sections.
The meaning of this is fully exhausted.
Because it is not urgent,
I have not included it as a separate fascicle here.
The Catalogue of the Annotated Scriptures of the Tiantai Commentaries, comprising fifty-five volumes in seventy-five fascicles, includes the following Mahāyāna sūtras:

the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in seven fascicles; the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra* in three fascicles; the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* in thirty-eight fascicles; the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-sammukhāvasthita-samādhi-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Amitāyurdhyāna-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* (Smaller Amitābha Sūtra) in one fascicle; and the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* in four fascicles. These constitute the aforementioned Mahāyāna sūtras.
The structural analysis according to the Tiantai commentaries is hereby completed.
The catalog of Mahāyāna sūtras, vinayas, and dhāraṇīs consists of a total of thirteen works in nineteen fascicles.
*Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Susiddhi-sūtra*, three fascicles; *Subāhu-paripṛcchā-tantra*, three fascicles;

*New Translation of the Great Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle; *Prasannapadā Dhāraṇī* (The Dhāraṇī for Obtaining Whatever One Seeks) in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle;
*Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-vijaya Dhāraṇī* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle.
One fascicle of the Thousand-Armed Dhāraṇī in both Chinese and Sanskrit characters; one fascicle of the Thousand-Handed Dhāraṇī in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
one fascicle of the King of Spells Dhāraṇī of One Character in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters; one fascicle of the Five-Syllable Mañjuśrī Dhāraṇī in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
and one [fascicle] of the Maṇḍala of the Spontaneous Attainment of All Needs in both Chinese and Sanskrit characters.
One scroll of the Zhangfan Seed-Syllable Maṇḍala; one scroll of the Universal Maṇḍala of the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa;
and the catalogs for the miscellaneous transcriptions of other schools.
The miscellaneous transcriptions of other schools comprise twenty-two lacquered volumes and one thousand six hundred thirty-five sheets.

The *Commentary on the Four-Part Vinaya* (Sifen lü chao ji), nineteen fascicles, one thousand three hundred and eighty sheets; the *Exegesis on the Fourteen Topics* (Shisi ke yi shu), two fascicles, one hundred and twenty sheets; the *Extracts on the Fourteen Topics* (Shisi ke yi chao), one fascicle, sixty-six sheets; the *Exegesis on Hetuvidyā* (Inming shu) with annotations, two fascicles, sixty-three sheets; and the *Hetuvidyā* (Inming) with annotations, one fascicle, sixty-three sheets; and the *Ritual for Buddhist Fasts* (Shishi zhai yi), one fascicle, twenty sheets; and the *Record of the Ritual for Buddhist Fasts* (Shishi zhai yi ji), one fascicle, twenty-five sheets. These five works, totaling eight fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
Three items of miscellaneous objects:

one *dhyāna-sthapanī* (meditation support) with a single head, one *dharmacakra-śveta-viṣāṇa* (Dharma-wheel white-horn) *cintāmaṇi* (wish-fulfilling gem) handle, and four pieces of *tso-ch’ih* wood from Mount Xiangluo Peak on Mount Tiantai, including two pieces of *tso-ch’ih* wood marked with the *wen-chi* (measuring scale) pattern. Postscript: The above items were explained by the Great Master Zhizhe of Mount Tiantai in the Mahayana sutras and other texts.
Along with the recorded traces of the teachings he expounded,
as well as the biographies of the Second, Fifth, and Sixth Patriarchs,
and various other compilations.
In total, there are one hundred and twenty works comprising three hundred and forty-five fascicles,
excluding the paper used for the physical records of the scriptures.
Eight thousand five hundred and thirty-two sheets.
Saichō and others received them with profound gratitude;
they were produced by the Court Gentleman (Nangō) Jizō.
Copied according to the original count at the Jingtuyuan (Pure Land Cloister) of Longxing Temple in Linhai County, Taizhou, during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Having completed the collation and verification,
I respectfully request the official seal of this prefecture.
This is shown to later students so that they may know where to seek the Dharma.
Thus, the virtue of the Magistrate’s gift of the Dharma is [immeasurable].
Eternal and boundless,
it is the function of the functions of the dharmas of sentient beings;
throughout the long night, it never ceases.
I pray that the brilliance of the transmission of the Dharma may shine forth,
and that this merit be dedicated so that the Governor’s blessings increase in every thought-moment and perfect wisdom be realized in each instant.
Thereafter, they shall extend universally to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions,
so that all may ride together upon a single precious chariot and travel the Eightfold Noble Path,
regarding enemies and kin with equal impartiality.
For both himself and others.

Recorded on the nineteenth day, the second month, the year of Yǒuyǒu (Bǐyǒu), the twenty-first year of the Zhēnyuán era of the Great Táng, the cyclical sign being Bǐyǒu, by the Dharma-seeking monk Saichō of Hiei-zan-ji in the Kingdom of Japan, together with the Dharma-seeking and translation-assisting monk Gishin, the Dharma-seeking attendant Tanfukujō, the presiding Abbot of the Enryaku-ji on Mount Tiantái in the Great Táng, the Xījīng Wànsì (Western Capital Monastery) Monk Dōsui, and the Acharya Saichō.
Though their physical forms belong to different realms,
their natures truly share a common source;
they have uniquely received the gift of innate wisdom.
He attained an immediate and comprehensive understanding of all categories of phenomena, seeking afar the sublime essence of the celestial teachings,
and further encountered the eminent Master Sui, a true dragon and elephant among men.
He unified the myriad practices within a single mind and thoroughly understood the three contemplations as divergent paths;
he received the secret teachings directly from the Buddha.
The principle transcends names and words;
yet, fearing that students from other regions might be unable to believe and accept it,
I have requested an official seal from this province to certify it.
How could this not be relied upon as authoritative?
On the twentieth day of the second month in the twenty-first year of the Zhenyuan era of the Great Tang,
Chao Yi, Acting Military Commissioner of the Various Military Affairs of Taizhou, Acting Prefect of Taizhou, and Marquis of Shangzhuoguo, respectfully sent this letter.
The Japanese Envoys to Tang China:
The Chief Envoy, holding the insignia of authority, of the fourth rank, upper class, Right Great Counselor of the Grand Council of State, concurrently Governor of Yuefeng, Fujiwara no Asomi Kazuno;
The Acting Vice Envoy, concurrently Translator, of the sixth rank, upper class, Assistant Official of Bizen, [Fujiwara no Asomi].
Kasa: Minister Tada, Recorder of the Sixth Rank Upper Grade, Acting Assistant Registrar of the Ministry of Ceremonial (Shikibushō), concurrently Great Overseer of Ise, Merit Rank Six.
Yamada-no-tsu: Daitei, Recorder of the Sixth Rank Upper Grade, Left Assistant Historian of the Grand Council of State (Taizōkan), concurrently Junior Overseer of Hitachi.
Kōno no Tamehito (Upper Ōmi-no-kami) was a man of distinguished character.
